key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface potentials more uniform and dynamically stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage response.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can be used to lower nonradiative losses and improve stability in perovskite solar-cell interfaces.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) and light-induced surface photovoltage (SPV) before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Analyze wavelength-dependent SPV and separate grain-boundary vs grain-interior contributions
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: These are nanoscale surface measurements on thin films, so device-level performance gains and long-term operational stability still need direct confirmation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
